name: Kagawa Prefectural Police × Kagawa University Joint Shoplifting Prevention Programme
summary: A long-running collaboration beginning in 2010, developing from surveys to manuals, education, implementation in retail settings and subsequent evaluation.

name: Fukuoka Prefectural Police Crime Prevention Research Adviser Programme
researchOrganizations: Researchers from the University of Tsukuba, the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, Kyushu University, Saga University, Hokuriku University and other institutions
summary: Established in November 2014. The programme has produced Research Findings Reports No. 1 and No. 2 as well as a number of related publications.

name: Kyoto Prefectural Police Crime Deterrence Research Committee
themes: Crime prevention and deterrence measures, including responses to sexual offences
summary: Research subgroups, including a sexual-offence research group, have linked crime-data analysis with practical measures such as mobile CCTV and lighting. Further detailed reports remain a priority for continued searching.

name: Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department Expert Committee on the Safety of Children and Women
researchOrganizations: Researchers in criminology, geography, urban planning, psychology and related fields
themes: Prevention of crime victimisation among children and women
summary: The committee has considered data analysis, public communication, crime prevention education, environmental design and related measures.

name: Osaka Prefectural Police Collaborative Research Group for Advanced Crime Prevention
researchOrganizations: Researchers from Otemon Gakuin University, the University of Tsukuba and other institutions
summary: A continuing collaboration aimed at developing crime prevention grounded in scientific evidence, including work on VR materials, leaflets, posters and methods for evaluating preventive interventions.

name: Shiga Prefectural Police × Osaka University Behavioural-Economics Nudge Implementation Partnership
themes: Applying behavioural economics and nudges to crime prevention
summary: A formal partnership established in 2023 that has developed into field experiments addressing issues including bicycle theft.

name: Kanagawa Prefectural Police Collaborative Research Group on Crime and Traffic-Collision Analysis
researchOrganizations: University of Tsukuba and other institutions
summary: Academic researchers participate as committee members. Individual intervention studies arising from the collaboration remain a target for further identification.

name: Kochi Prefectural Police × Three Kochi Universities and Partners Bicycle-Theft Research Programme
researchOrganizations: University of Kochi, Kochi University of Technology, Kochi University and Shiga University
summary: A collaborative programme progressing from data analysis and interviews to a cluster randomised controlled trial.

name: Fukushima Prefectural Police Experimental Research with Crime Prevention Advisers
researchOrganizations: Fukushima University, Shiga University and other institutions
summary: Field evaluations of crime prevention measures in bicycle-parking areas and retail settings, including nudge signage, banners and voice-message interventions.

name: Shiga Prefectural Police × Shiga University Research Committee on Fraud Prevention
summary: An ongoing collaboration planning analysis of police-held data together with field experiments and other evaluations.

name: Nara Crime Prevention Psychology Research Group
researchOrganizations: Nara University, Nara Women's University, Tezukayama University, Shiga University and Osaka Kyoiku University
themes: Investment and romance scams conducted through social media and related offences
summary: A collaborative research group applying psychological evidence to the design and evaluation of prevention measures.

name: Fukuyama University Criminal Psychology Laboratory × Hiroshima Prefectural Police Community Safety Mapping and Youth Support Collaboration
summary: The collaboration began in the 2000s and continued after 2010 through community safety mapping, student crime prevention activities and youth support. Individual published intervention evaluations remain a target for further identification.

name: Fukuyama University × Hiroshima Prefectural Police Traffic Safety Project and Joint Research Programme
summary: A broad traffic-safety research collaboration established in 2015. Work reported in 2017 included physiological measurement, immersive driving simulation and research on blue and white street lighting. It is retained as a field adjacent to crime prevention research.

name: KAKENHI Scientific Research (S) 20H05632: Policy Applications of Behavioural Economics in Health, Disaster Prevention, Crime Prevention, Labour and Education
policeOrganizations: Includes crime prevention research conducted with the National Research Institute of Police Science, Shiga Prefectural Police and other police partners
researchOrganizations: Osaka University, led by Fumio Ohtake, together with researchers from the National Research Institute of Police Science and other institutions
summary: A major 2020–2024 research project explicitly including crime prevention. Researchers included Takahito Shimada, Tomonori Saito and Yuko Yamane. It provides a useful parent project for tracing behavioural-economics interventions concerning fraud, voyeurism and other crime prevention problems.
